mainTopic: Mixtures: blood of a קרבן mixed with other liquids, and forbidden foods that cancel each other out
overview: The amud first finishes the משנה about blood that got mixed with other things. רבי יהודה holds that blood never cancels out other blood. Good blood mixed with blood of פסולין, or with דם התמצית, is poured into the drain. רבי אליעזר allows the תמצית mixture, and if the כהן already put it on the מזבח without asking, the קרבן still counts. In the גמרא, רבי יוחנן says the 'looks like blood' rule works only when water fell into blood; blood that drips into water is cancelled drop by drop. רב פפא adds that this is not so for כיסוי הדם, because אין דחוי במצוות. Then ריש לקיש rules that someone who eats a mixture of פיגול, נותר and טמא meat gets no מלקות, and the גמרא learns three rules from him. רבא attacks one of those rules, that נותן טעם with a majority is not from the Torah, using a משנה about a wheat-and-rice dough. The answer that the חלה obligation is only מדרבנן runs into the end of that משנה, which lets this dough count for the Torah מצוה of מצה. The discussion of this challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Blood does not cancel out blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the earlier part of the משנה and says that one kind of blood can never cancel out another kind of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Blood does not cancel out blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its list of mixtures. Here רבי יהודה gives his own opinion: when blood mixes with blood, none of it is cancelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה (on the previous daf), the תנא קמא said that when two kinds of blood mix, we picture one of them as if it were water and judge by that. רבי יהודה rejects this. In his view blood stays blood, so the mixture still has enough proper blood and the כהן may put it on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels out; makes something lose its own identity inside a mixture
Blood, here the blood of a קרבן that goes on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Blood does not cancel out blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין דָּם מְבַטֵּל דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling (on the previous daf) about blood mixed with blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a mixture, one blood never cancels out another blood.

steps.title: Mixed with unfit blood or with seeping blood
steps.stepSummary: If good blood got mixed with blood of פסולין or with דם התמצית, the whole mixture is poured into the drain. רבי אליעזר allows the תמצית mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it got mixed with the blood of unfit offerings, it is poured into the drain. If it got mixed with seeping blood, it is poured into the drain; רבי אליעזר says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more mixture cases. In both, the תנא קמא says to throw the whole mixture away, and רבי אליעזר disagrees about the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from פסולין can never go on the מזבח, so once it is mixed in there is nothing to fix and the mixture is poured out. דם התמצית is also not fit for the מזבח, so the תנא קמא treats it the same way. רבי אליעזר holds that this mixture is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: קרבנות that became unfit, whose blood may not go on the מזבח
The drain channel running through the עזרה
Blood that drips out slowly after the main spurt at שחיטה
Rules it valid

phrases.english: If it got mixed with the blood of unfit offerings,
it should be poured into the drain.
phrases.notes: The אמה is a water channel in the courtyard of the בית המקדש that carried things away.

phrases.english: With seeping blood,
phrases.notes: This is the blood that oozes out after the first strong spurt, which is not fit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: it should be poured into the drain;
Rabbi Eliezer rules it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from blood-with-blood to blood mixed with blood that is not fit for the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixture with פסולין blood or דם התמצית is poured out; רבי אליעזר allows the תמצית mixture.

steps.title: If the כהן already placed it, it is valid
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן did not ask the חכמים and simply put the mixed blood on the מזבח, the קרבן is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not consult and placed it, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying what happens after the fact. A כהן who went ahead and put the blood on the מזבח without asking has a valid קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between what you should do from the start (לכתחילה), which is to pour the mixture away, and what counts once it is done (בדיעבד). Even the תנא קמא agrees that once the blood was placed, the קרבן works.

keyTerms.meaning: Consulted; asked the חכמים what to do
Valid, fit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is now letting you put this blood on the מזבח from the start. The instruction is still to pour it out; this line only tells you the result if it was already done.

phrases.english: If he did not consult and placed it,
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the כהן, who put the blood on the מזבח without first asking the חכמים.

phrases.english: it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the after-the-fact ruling to the 'pour it out' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the fact, if the כהן placed the mixed blood without asking, the קרבן is כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two levels: from the start, pour the mixture out; after the fact, if it was already placed, the קרבן is valid.

steps.title: Only when water fell into blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's rule about water and blood. It only applies when water fell into blood. If blood fell into water, each drop is cancelled out as it lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only when water fell into blood. But if blood fell into water, each first drop is cancelled out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן narrows the משנה's ruling that a water-and-blood mixture is fit if it still looks like blood: it only covers the case where water was poured into blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When water falls into blood, there is a body of blood from the start, and the water joins it. When blood drips into water, each single drop is swamped by the water and cancelled right away, one after another. So the blood is already lost, and the mixture is פסול even if it ends up looking like blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
They only taught this in the case of...; a phrase that limits a ruling
Each drop is cancelled out as it lands
Cancelled out, lost inside the mixture

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the order in which things mix can decide whether something is בטל, not just how the final mixture looks.

phrases.english: Gemara.
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only
where water fell into blood,
but if blood fell into water,
each first drop is cancelled out.
phrases.notes: Literally 'first, first is cancelled': every drop is lost in the water the moment it falls in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier part of the משנה (water mixed with blood) and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'looks like blood' rule applies only when water fell into blood. When blood fell into water, it is cancelled drop by drop.

steps.title: For covering the blood, the rule is different
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that for the מצוה of כיסוי הדם, blood that fell into water is not lost, because אין דחוי במצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: But regarding covering the blood, it is not so, because there is no permanent pushing-aside in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a limit to רבי יוחנן's rule. For כיסוי הדם, even blood that dripped into water must still be covered if the mixture looks like blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a קרבן, once each drop is cancelled, it is pushed aside for good. For כיסוי, a drop that was cancelled is only pushed aside for a moment. Once enough blood gathers that the mixture looks like blood, the מצוה comes back, because אין דחוי במצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or חיה
It is not so; the rule here is different
A מצוה is not permanently pushed aside; it can come back

steps.whatToRemember: Blood dripping into water is lost drop by drop for a קרבן, but for כיסוי הדם it still must be covered if the mixture looks like blood, because אין דחוי במצוות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. רבי יוחנן's 'cancelled drop by drop' rule is for blood on the מזבח; רב פפא says it does not apply to covering the blood.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
But regarding covering, it is not so,
phrases.notes: This is covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal (ויקרא 17:13).

phrases.english: because there is no permanent pushing-aside in מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּלְעִנְיַן כִּיסּוּי אֵינוֹ כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's drop-by-drop rule so it does not apply to כיסוי הדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For כיסוי הדם, blood that fell into water still must be covered if the mixture looks like blood, since אין דחוי במצוות.

steps.title: Eating a mixture of three forbidden meats brings no lashes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that someone who eats a mixture of פיגול, נותר and טמא meat is פטור from מלקות, because one type will always outweigh another and cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: If someone mixed together פיגול, נותר and impure meat and ate them, he is exempt. It is impossible that one type will not be more than another and cancel it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from ריש לקיש about mixing different forbidden meats together. He says the person who eats the mixture does not get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three meats is forbidden by its own separate איסור. Once they are mixed, whichever type is bigger in each bite cancels the smaller one. Nobody can know in advance which איסור the person will end up breaking, so he cannot get a clear warning, and without a clear warning there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made with the intent to eat it after its allowed time
Meat of a קרבן left over after its eating time ran out
Ritually impure (here, impure קרבן meat)
Exempt from punishment
Cancelling out: a smaller amount loses its identity inside a bigger amount

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not say the mixture is allowed to eat. He only says the eater is not given מלקות.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Piggul, notar, and impure meat
that one mixed together, one with the other
phrases.notes: He is picturing a full כזית of each kind, enough for lashes on its own, all mixed up together.

phrases.english: and ate them: he is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יַרְבֶּה מִין עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: it is impossible that one type will not be more than another
and cancel it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixtures of blood to a new case of mixed forbidden meats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who eats a mixture of פיגול, נותר and טמא is פטור from מלקות, because one type always cancels another.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws three rules from ריש לקיש. Forbidden foods can cancel each other. נותן טעם with a majority is not a Torah law. A doubtful warning does not count as a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. First, forbidden things cancel each other out. Second, the rule that a taste forbids even when outnumbered is not from the Torah. Third, an uncertain warning is not considered a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out three general rules that must be true for ריש לקיש's ruling to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, ריש לקיש lets one איסור cancel another איסור, so cancelling is not only done by permitted food. Second, each meat surely gives taste to the others, yet he does not give lashes, so the taste rule with a majority must be only מדרבנן. Third, the witnesses could only give a 'maybe' warning, and he gives no lashes, so a doubtful warning does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (introduces a lesson drawn from a source)
Forbidden foods cancel each other out
Gives taste: forbidden food that flavors the mixture
From the Torah
A doubtful warning, given when it is not clear which איסור will be broken

steps.whatToRemember: Hold on to the second lesson: נותן טעם with a majority is only מדרבנן. That is the lesson רבא is about to attack.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אִיסּוּרִין מְבַטְּלִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: learn from it that forbidden things cancel each other out,
and learn from it that giving taste when there is a majority
is not from the Torah,
and learn from it that an uncertain warning
is not called a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws general rules out of ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Forbidden foods cancel each other. נותן טעם with a majority is only מדרבנן. A doubtful warning is not a warning.

steps.title: רבא challenges with a dough of wheat and rice
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה: a wheat-and-rice dough that tastes of grain needs חלה even though most of it is rice. So it seems taste does matter when it is outnumbered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: If someone made a dough from wheat and rice, and it has the taste of grain, it must have חלה taken from it. This is so even though most of it is rice!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the second lesson, that taste with a majority is not a Torah law. He uses a משנה about mixed dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rice does not need חלה, but wheat does. The wheat is the smaller part, yet because it gives the dough a grain taste, the whole dough needs חלה. This looks like the taste of the smaller part really counts, which goes against what we just learned from ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough
Rice (not one of the five grains)
The portion of dough given to a כהן
The majority

phrases.english: Rava objects:

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה עִיסָּה מִן חִיטִּין וּמִן אוֹרֶז –
phrases.english: If one made a dough from wheat and from rice,
if it has the taste of grain,
it is obligated in challah.
And this is so even though most of it is rice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second lesson of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson that נותן טעם with a majority is not a Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A minority of wheat makes the whole dough need חלה because of its taste, so taste seems to count even when outnumbered.

steps.title: The חלה obligation there is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dough needs חלה only מדרבנן, so the משנה tells us nothing about Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The obligation is from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא in one word: the חלה rule for this dough is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the obligation is only rabbinic, the חכמים simply added a rule because of the grain taste. That does not show the Torah treats taste with a majority as counting, so the lesson from ריש לקיש still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not Torah law

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrades the source's ruling to rabbinic level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חלה obligation shows the Torah counts taste even when outnumbered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חלה obligation is only מדרבנן, so it proves nothing about Torah law.

steps.title: The end of the משנה lets this dough be used for the Torah מצוה of מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back. The same משנה says one fulfills the מצוה of מצה on פסח with this dough, and that מצוה is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of that משנה: a person fulfills his obligation with this dough on פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the answer by quoting the end of the same משנה. The obligation it deals with is clearly from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating מצה on the first night of פסח is a Torah מצוה, and it can only be done with grain. If this mostly-rice dough works for it because of the wheat taste, then taste is counting on a Torah level. So the answer 'it is מדרבנן' does not fit the whole משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (turns the answer against itself)
Say the last part of the source
Fulfills his obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge puts the second lesson from ריש לקיש back in doubt, and the sugya will have to deal with it next.

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
A person fulfills his obligation with it
on Pesach!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 using the end of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the dough's status is only מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה lets this dough count for the Torah מצוה of מצה, so its grain status, based on taste, must be from the Torah.
